Delivery, not the service, carries it on one route for the live change and the catch-up. So every panel sees a service go down or come back, and a panel opened late sees the same. cards.designTerms: Equipment should own one dated record per capability behind one interface that reports value, health and age, with MPD an adapter beneath; Delivery should own the single route, one builder per fact for live and catch-up, carrying the label. Today the seam leaks: the broadcast module re-implements each service's change set as a per-domain event list, so the interface callers must know is the full event list, and locality is lost.
cards.standaloneLine: In a standalone game: no venue service runs, so no fault today; the tablet hides its panels and the player devices hold none. In the shape the tablet's Equipment stand-in reports every duty dormant, so a panel can say "not tonight" instead of vanishing (candidate A); with its own engine the panels stay hidden (B).
cards.shapeChange: The record moved from the music service to Equipment, which dates it. The push moved to Delivery, which reads every change and sends it on one route. So when Home Assistant or MPD goes down or comes back, every panel changes with no reload, and a tablet that connects late sees the same. The panel now shows the record's age. The other option is now the shape's: each job keeps its own pushes.
